00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:12.760: A sustained, resonant bell tone, low-pitched and metallic, rings out with a long decay, filling the space with a slow, vibrating hum. No speech is present.

00:00:12.760 --> 00:00:13.500: The bell tone fades out completely. Silence follows.

00:00:13.500 --> 00:00:14.500: A male voice begins speaking, clear and measured, saying: “What is Nirvana?”

00:00:14.500 --> 00:00:22.500: The same male voice continues: “Nibbana is when everything the mind makes comes to a stop. The letting go of everything carried, the thirst ends, nothing pulls you anymore, stopping.”

00:00:22.500 --> 00:00:28.500: The voice continues: “Going out like a flame with no fuel.”

00:00:28.500 --> 00:00:35.500: The voice continues: “This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.”

00:00:35.500 --> 00:00:37.500: A brief pause. No speech.

00:00:37.500 --> 00:00:39.500: A different male voice begins: “Why don’t I see Nirvana right now?”

00:00:39.500 --> 00:00:48.500: The second voice continues: “You do not see Nibbana right now because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there.”

00:00:48.500 --> 00:00:56.500: The second voice continues: “What is called ‘manana’ is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things.”

00:00:56.500 --> 00:01:04.500: The second voice continues: “Only looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only seeing is there, nothing to be seen.”

00:01:04.500 --> 00:01:11.500: The second voice continues: “The law of dependent arising is already implicated. There is therefore no seer apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathagata.”

00:01:11.500 --> 00:01:13.500: A brief pause. No speech.

00:01:13.500 --> 00:01:15.500: The first voice returns: “What keeps it going?”

00:01:15.500 --> 00:01:22.500: The first voice continues: “Thirst keeps it going, impelled by that making it into something, it runs towards the mirage, the gap is ignored, what impels one to ignore that gap is thirst.”
